text:
Oliver Bonk is earning real minutes in his first full NHL season: about 18.7 a night for a rookie who had played one NHL game before this year. NHL.com's Rookie Watch put him alongside Anaheim's Caulfield as a young defender earning trust, and Broad Street Hockey wondered whether Philadelphia underestimated his offence. Seven points in 14 games (six in his last ten) makes the case.

Our numbers think he's been unlucky, not lucky. The Flyers have scored 5.9 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and his own finishing is right on expected. The concern is the same as for the team around him: Philadelphia gets out-chanced with him at five on five (45.7%), though less so than without him. The 22nd pick of 2023 is ahead of the history for his draft slot: among defencemen picked 17th to 27th since 2005, the median first full season is 0.21 points a game, and 30 of 65 reached 200 games. Our range on him is wide, but the middle projection is around 36 points.
